title: Why Don't Touchscreens Work With Gloves? #Shorts
description:
Why don't touchscreens work with gloves? Under the glass is a grid of tiny invisible wires holding a little electric charge. Your skin conducts, so when you touch the screen some of that charge flows into your finger, and the grid feels the dip right at that spot. That's your tap. Wool and leather don't conduct, so the charge has nowhere to go and the screen can't tell you're there. Touchscreen gloves fix it with conductive thread sewn into the fingertips. (And yes, a sausage works too. Please don't.)

Explained in 60, podcast edition
